eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Manila’s June 16, 2026 daily maximum temperature centers on 33–35 °C because official PAGASA guidance and multiple model runs converge in that narrow band while monsoon dynamics introduce day-of uncertainty.**

PAGASA’s extended outlook lists a 25–33 °C range with a 40 % rain chance for Metro Manila on the 16th, reflecting the early southwest monsoon (habagat) that typically brings increased cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and moderating sea-breeze effects from Manila Bay. Ensemble and private forecasts, however, show slight upward bias to 34–35 °C when daytime insolation remains strong before convective clouds build, consistent with the market’s 41 % and 35.5 % probabilities on those two outcomes.

The key scientific differentiators are afternoon cloud timing and boundary-layer moisture. Thicker monsoon cloud decks or early thunderstorms can suppress the maximum by 1–2 °C through reduced solar heating and evaporative cooling, favoring the 33 °C bin. Conversely, delayed convection or a temporary monsoon break allows greater surface heating and urban heat-island amplification in the densely built metro area, pushing readings to 34–35 °C. Humidity and wind shifts from the prevailing southwesterlies further modulate the heat index but have less direct impact on the dry-bulb maximum used for market resolution. With the day already underway and new model updates or surface observations still possible, the tight spread between the top three outcomes captures this genuine short-term forecast uncertainty.

**Trader sentiment for Kuala Lumpur’s June 17 maximum temperature centers on 31–33 °C because long-range and short-range models place the most likely peak near the June climatological average of 32 °C.** 

AccuWeather and other guidance show daily highs ranging 30.5–33.4 °C through the month, with June 17 specifically projected near 31–32 °C (roughly 88–90 °F) under the prevailing southwest monsoon. Afternoon convective showers and variable cloud cover are the main variables that can suppress or allow a brief spike to 33 °C; clearer skies or delayed rain would favor the higher end, while earlier or heavier convection favors 31 °C. Historical early-June observations near 33–35 °C illustrate the upper tail, but current model consensus and the typical 12–13 rainy days per month keep probabilities tightly clustered around the middle outcomes. Updated NWP runs and official Malaysian Meteorological Department guidance ahead of the 17th remain the key near-term catalysts.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
